content.text:
Four households have a 2025 wash sale: **HH-0363, HH-0780, HH-0129 and HH-9234**. One more, **HH-3058**, can't be settled from these files.

**How I checked.** I went through every 2025 sale in all 92 households. Only individual and joint taxable accounts count; sales in IRAs, inherited IRAs and 401(k)s were left out. The custodian's realized-lot files show 11 taxable sales at a loss in 2025. For each one I looked for any purchase or RSU vest of the same security, in any account in the household, within 30 days before or after the sale date. I then confirmed in `household.json` that whoever owned the buying account was the seller or the seller's spouse.

**The four wash sales.** In each case a couple sold from their joint taxable account and bought the same fund again in one spouse's IRA. Only part of the position was bought back, so only that share of the loss is disallowed (loss × units bought ÷ units sold):

| Household | Sale (date, units, loss) | Replacement (date, units, account) | Days after | Disallowed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0363 | T-0363-0035, 21 Oct, 3,192 Brackwater Dividend Equity Fund, −$35,820.62 | T-0363-0037, 3 Nov, 1,340 Brackwater Dividend Equity Fund, Anika's IRA | 13 | **$15,037.48** |
| HH-0780 | T-0780-0022, 4 Sep, 879 Larkspur Developed Markets Fund, −$12,860.65 | T-0780-0031, 2 Oct, 390 Larkspur Developed Markets Fund, Nadia's IRA | 28 | **$5,706.09** |
| HH-0129 | T-0129-0035, 3 Oct, 642 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, −$31,896.36 | T-0129-0037, 15 Oct, 360 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, Jun's Roth IRA | 12 | **$17,885.81** |
| HH-9234 | T-9234-0035, 3 Nov, 847 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, −$53,516.17 | T-9234-0037, 19 Nov, 500 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, Ingrid's IRA | 16 | **$31,591.60** |

The replacements are all in IRAs. Under IRS Revenue Ruling 2008-5, the disallowed loss is not added to the cost of the IRA shares, so it is lost for good rather than deferred.

**Close calls that are not wash sales.** These buybacks fell just outside the 30 days:
- HH-9571 and HH-0679: 31 days after the sale.
- HH-0380: 35 days.
- HH-0981: 37 days.
- HH-0847 and HH-0420: 41 days.
- HH-0514: 55 days.

**Unresolved: HH-3058.** On 12 Dec 2025 (T-3058-0048), 1,600 Bramwell Devices Group were sold from the stock-plan account. The custodian has no cost basis for the two RSU lots sold (vested 20 Feb and 20 May). Their value on the vest dates isn't recorded anywhere in the files, so I can't tell whether the sale was a loss. Another 800 Bramwell Devices Group vested on 20 Nov (T-3058-0047), 22 days before the sale. If the sale was a loss, that vest would be a replacement. The other stock-plan sales with no recorded basis (HH-0816, HH-0221, HH-0376) had no acquisition within 30 days, so they can't be wash sales whatever their basis.

result:
Four households have a 2025 wash sale: **HH-0363, HH-0780, HH-0129 and HH-9234**. One more, **HH-3058**, can't be settled from these files.

**How I checked.** I went through every 2025 sale in all 92 households. Only individual and joint taxable accounts count; sales in IRAs, inherited IRAs and 401(k)s were left out. The custodian's realized-lot files show 11 taxable sales at a loss in 2025. For each one I looked for any purchase or RSU vest of the same security, in any account in the household, within 30 days before or after the sale date. I then confirmed in `household.json` that whoever owned the buying account was the seller or the seller's spouse.

**The four wash sales.** In each case a couple sold from their joint taxable account and bought the same fund again in one spouse's IRA. Only part of the position was bought back, so only that share of the loss is disallowed (loss × units bought ÷ units sold):

| Household | Sale (date, units, loss) | Replacement (date, units, account) | Days after | Disallowed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HH-0363 | T-0363-0035, 21 Oct, 3,192 Brackwater Dividend Equity Fund, −$35,820.62 | T-0363-0037, 3 Nov, 1,340 Brackwater Dividend Equity Fund, Anika's IRA | 13 | **$15,037.48** |
| HH-0780 | T-0780-0022, 4 Sep, 879 Larkspur Developed Markets Fund, −$12,860.65 | T-0780-0031, 2 Oct, 390 Larkspur Developed Markets Fund, Nadia's IRA | 28 | **$5,706.09** |
| HH-0129 | T-0129-0035, 3 Oct, 642 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, −$31,896.36 | T-0129-0037, 15 Oct, 360 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, Jun's Roth IRA | 12 | **$17,885.81** |
| HH-9234 | T-9234-0035, 3 Nov, 847 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, −$53,516.17 | T-9234-0037, 19 Nov, 500 Wexcombe Mid Cap Fund, Ingrid's IRA | 16 | **$31,591.60** |

The replacements are all in IRAs. Under IRS Revenue Ruling 2008-5, the disallowed loss is not added to the cost of the IRA shares, so it is lost for good rather than deferred.

**Close calls that are not wash sales.** These buybacks fell just outside the 30 days:
- HH-9571 and HH-0679: 31 days after the sale.
- HH-0380: 35 days.
- HH-0981: 37 days.
- HH-0847 and HH-0420: 41 days.
- HH-0514: 55 days.

**Unresolved: HH-3058.** On 12 Dec 2025 (T-3058-0048), 1,600 Bramwell Devices Group were sold from the stock-plan account. The custodian has no cost basis for the two RSU lots sold (vested 20 Feb and 20 May). Their value on the vest dates isn't recorded anywhere in the files, so I can't tell whether the sale was a loss. Another 800 Bramwell Devices Group vested on 20 Nov (T-3058-0047), 22 days before the sale. If the sale was a loss, that vest would be a replacement. The other stock-plan sales with no recorded basis (HH-0816, HH-0221, HH-0376) had no acquisition within 30 days, so they can't be wash sales whatever their basis.
